text:
jess: Heads-up — perfetto captures for kvcache hotspots are missing source line numbers when run from our distroless runtime image. nsys shows function names but aux lineinfo is empty. Repro'd on a Dedicated-rt pod. cc @mike @zara

mike: Do we strip debug info in the packaging step? Check CI Dockerfile for `strip --strip-debug` or `eu-strip`.

zara: We currently run `eu-strip` in the final stage and use distroless. We also don't ship /usr/lib/debug into the image.

ryan: Another common culprit: CUPTI/driver mismatch. If the CUPTI that nsys uses doesn't match host driver/libs it can fail to resolve lines. What driver/CUPTI on the node?

jess: Node driver is 535.12, CUPTI artifacts in our build image are from cuda 12.0 — mismatch suspected. But I repro'd a host-side nsys run and lines were present, only containerized runs lacked line numbers.

mike: Steps to debug:
- run `nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt --output=kv.qdrep ./server --workload` inside the container
- `nsys export -f perfetto -i kv.qdrep -o kv.perfetto` and open in perfetto UI
- use `addr2line -e /path/to/binary 0x<addr>` against host's debug binary to confirm line mapping

zara: FWIW we saw a path-mapping issue before: build-id paths inside the binary point to host-installed locations and the container has relocated FS layout so nsys can't find the debuginfo. Binding host /usr/lib/debug into the container fixed it for that case.

jess: Quick repro attempts: ran nsys on the host (outside container) -> line numbers present. Ran same nsys command inside distroless container -> function names only, no line numbers. So this is a symbolization look-up problem, not the profiler itself.

ryan: Two immediate mitigation options:
1) Produce a separate debug image / debug tarball that contains the unstripped binaries or `*.debug` files and bind-mount them at `/usr/lib/debug` at runtime when profiling.
2) Change CI to keep a debug artifact (debuglink / .build_id mapping) alongside the release image and add docs for how to attach it for profiling.

mike: Also verify build-ids match: `readelf -n /path/to/binary` and `eu-readelf -n /usr/lib/debug/.build-id/...`. If build-id matches, nsys should resolve lines when debug files are available.

jess: I pushed a debug variant branch (no-strip) and a CI change that uploads a debug tarball. Can someone run perftrace against `redwood/rt:dev-debug` and upload the qdrep?

zara: I'll run it. Command I'll use: 
```
docker run --rm --cap-add=SYS_ADMIN --security-opt seccomp=unconfined -v /tmp/debug:/debug redwood/rt:dev-debug bash -c "nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt --output=/tmp/kv.qdrep ./server --workload"
nsys export -f perfetto -i /tmp/kv.qdrep -o /tmp/kv.perfetto
```
I'll attach the qdrep + perfetto export.

perf-bot: uploaded artifact: /artifacts/perf/1765432100/kv.qdrep (size: 18.2MB)

ryan: When you upload, include the `nsys` metadata: `nsys stats -i kv.qdrep` and `readelf --notes` outputs for both the binary and the debug files so we can compare build-id/path mapping.

mike: One more edge-case: distroless images sometimes don't include correct CUPTI libs, so at runtime nsys falls back to limited symbolization. Try bind-mounting the host's `/usr/local/cuda/extras/CUPTI/lib64` into the container's matching path, or set `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` to point to the bundled CUPTI matching the GPU driver.

jess: Update: after bind-mounting `/usr/lib/debug` from the host into the container, line numbers returned. So root cause for this run = missing debuginfo accessible from inside container. Still have the CUPTI mismatch on some nodes to follow up separately.

zara: Great. Note: do not include debug artifacts in prod images. We'll keep debug tarball/artifact separate and provide instructions to mount during profiling.

jess: Filing follow-up: PERF-229 — add debug build variant + CI debug artifact + docs for containerized profiling (how to mount debug files and CUPTI libs). PR #457 points to the branch. Thanks everyone for quick triage :thumbsup:

mike: Thanks — adding test case to our perf regression suite to detect missing lineinfo for containerized runs.

ryan: If anyone hits this again, ping me and I'll help collect `nsys`/`perfetto` exports.

jess: closing loop here.
